- Black plays Qxd5 (captures the queen +9)
- White plays Nxd5 (captures the queen -9)
- Black plays Bxb5 (captures bishop +3)
- White plays Nxb4 (captures bishop -3)
- Black plays Bxe2 (captures knight +3)
- Net: +3 for Black after all exchanges

This is a fork/double attack! When Black plays **Qxd5**, the queen forks the White bishop on b5 and the knight on c3. Though the knight captures on d5, Black's bishop recaptures and then wins material through the cascade of forced exchanges.

**Best move:** Qxd5

**Main line:** Qxd5 Nxd5 Bxb5 Nxb4 Bxe2

**Motif:** fork

**Coaching note:**
When your queen is attacked, look for forcing moves—especially checks and captures. Here, Qxd5 doesn't move away; instead, it counterattacks White's bishop and creates a fork-like pattern. After the exchanges, Black is up material. Always look for forcing counterplay instead of passively retreating.
